# Progress

A labelled bar showing how much of a task with a known end is done.

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `progress` |
| Family | loading |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Behavior

A `role="progressbar"` element with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`, named by its visible label. Determinate only. No primitive: it holds no state and takes no input.

- **Determinate only; an unknown end is Spinner's job** — An indeterminate bar and a spinner answer the same question — "something is happening, I don't know how long" — and two components for one answer means callers pick between them by taste. Progress exists for the other question: how far along is it. Keeping `value` required makes the bar mean something every time it is on screen; a bar that sometimes shows progress and sometimes only motion teaches readers to ignore it.
- **Progress is not a meter** — Disk usage, a password's strength, a quota: those are measurements on a scale, not a task heading toward done, and ARIA gives them a different role (`meter`) for that reason. A progress bar reading "80% of storage" tells a screen reader that something is 80% finished. A meter is a separate component, and not part of this gate.
- **A `div` with `role="progressbar"`, not the native `<progress>` element** — `<progress>` is styled through vendor pseudo-elements that differ between engines and cannot carry a transition on the fill, and it has no `aria-valuetext` equivalent of its own. The ARIA role is fully supported, and it lets `valueText` say "3 of 7 files" instead of "43 percent".
- **The label is required and visible** — A bar with no label is a decoration: the reader sees motion and cannot tell what is moving. The visible label is also the accessible name, through `aria-labelledby`, so sighted and screen-reader users are told the same thing.
- **It does not announce every change** — A progress bar updating every 200ms as a live region would read a number every time the screen reader paused. The role is enough for a reader who navigates to it to hear the current value. What does need announcing is completion — and that is the caller's message, usually a Toast or a Notice, because only the caller knows what "done" means.
- **The track is `theme.bg.muted`, not Slider's `theme.border.strong`** — Approved at gate 1 (decision C8, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md). Slider and Progress look alike and are split by role. A slider's empty track is part of a control — it shows how far the value can still go — so it takes the boundary tone tuned to the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control. A progress bar takes no input, and its empty track carries no information on its own: what the reader needs is the fill against it, which the pairing decision below covers. So the track is the recessed well `theme.bg.muted` is documented for, and a progress bar beside a slider does not read as something to drag.
- **Track thickness: size.track** — The bar is size.track, 4px, the same token Slider's track uses — one thickness for every linear value bar, so a progress bar and a slider side by side read as the same family. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).
- **The fill on its track is a verified pairing** — theme.accent-role.bg on theme.bg.muted is now a documented AA-nontext pairing in system.json, measured at 4.89:1 (light) and 7.75:1 (dark) against the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a graphical object, and re-verified against every brand theme by themes:check. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).
- **Web and native** — Web: a `div` with `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` when `valueText` is passed, and `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label. In forced-colors mode the fill takes the system `Highlight` colour so it stays visible. React Native: a `View` with `accessibilityRole="progressbar"` and `accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max, now: value, text: valueText }}`, labelled by `accessibilityLabel`. All props work on both; the fill transition is skipped on native when the OS reduce-motion setting is on. Rata-drawn, not the OS progress control (decision N5): React Native core no longer ships one on either platform, and a drawn `View` takes the same tokens as the web bar. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

## Props

Extends `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, ProgressOwnedAttribute>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | What is in progress, shown above the bar. |
| `value` | `number` | — | How much is done, from 0 to `max`. |
| `max?` | `number` | `100` | The value that means done. |
| `valueText?` | `string` | — | The value in the reader's own units, shown beside the label and announced instead of a percentage. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes, for placement and width. |

### `label`

```ts
label: string
```

What is in progress, shown above the bar.

**Use when**

- A noun phrase naming the task: "Uploading tokens.json", "Import".

**Don't use for**

- "Loading…" on its own. Say what is loading.

**Accessibility** The bar's accessible name, wired with `aria-labelledby`.

### `value`

```ts
value: number
```

How much is done, from 0 to `max`.

**Use when**

- The real count of done units — bytes, files, steps.

**Don't use for**

- A value that is not real. A bar that eases toward 90% to look busy is a spinner pretending to know something; use Spinner.

**Accessibility** Becomes `aria-valuenow`. Clamped to the range, so an overshoot does not announce 104 percent.

### `max`

```ts
max?: number = 100
```

The value that means done.

**Use when**

- The total of whatever `value` counts — `max={7}` for seven files.

**Don't use for**

- Converting to a percentage yourself. Pass the real total and let `valueText` say it in the reader's units.

**Accessibility** Becomes `aria-valuemax`.

### `valueText`

```ts
valueText?: string
```

The value in the reader's own units, shown beside the label and announced instead of a percentage.

**Use when**

- "3 of 7 files", "12 MB of 40 MB".

**Don't use for**

- Repeating the label. This is the amount, not the task.

**Accessibility** Becomes `aria-valuetext`. Without it, screen readers announce a percentage computed from `value` and `max`.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes, for placement and width.

**Use when**

- Setting the bar's width in the page's layout.

**Don't use for**

- Recolouring the fill. Status colours on a progress bar read as a verdict on the task; report the outcome in a message instead.

## Use cases

### A multi-file upload

A task with a countable end, which the reader is waiting on.

```tsx
<Progress label="Uploading assets" value={done} max={files.length} valueText={`${done} of ${files.length} files`} />
```

`max` is the real total and `valueText` says it in files rather than percent. Completion is announced by the caller — a Toast saying "7 files uploaded" — because the bar itself is not a live region.

### Reaching for the wrong component

A request whose duration nobody knows.

```tsx
<Progress label="Loading" value={fakeProgress} />
```

Don't. A value that is not real is a spinner pretending to know something — use `<Spinner label="Loading invoices" />`. Equally, storage used out of a quota is a meter, not progress.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Progress
        label="Uploading assets"
        value={3}
        max={7}
        valueText="3 of 7 files"
        className="pg-wide-specimen"
      />
```

## Token recipe

### base

A label above a track, with the filled part in the accent fill. The track is the recessed well `theme.bg.muted` is documented for, because a progress bar reports status and is not a control.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| track background | `theme.bg.muted — status, not interactive, so not Slider's theme.border.strong; see the track decision` |
| fill background | `theme.accent-role.bg — a verified AA-nontext pairing on theme.bg.muted (4.89:1 light, 7.75:1 dark)` |
| track block-size | `size.track` |
| track border-radius | `radius.pill` |
| fill border-radius | `radius.pill` |
| fill transition | `motion.duration.medium with motion.easing.standard, on inline-size; none under prefers-reduced-motion` |
| label font-size | `type.body.size` |
| label color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| value text font-size | `type.supporting.size` |
| value text color | `theme.fg.secondary` |
| gap between label row and track | `space.stack.2xs` |
